question.problem:
Let the joint CDF of $X$ and $Y$ be $F(x,y),$ where

$$
F(1,5)=0.63,\,F(0,5)=0.5,\,F(-2,5)=0.27.
$$

Find $P(-2\le X\le 1,Y\le 5).$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that $F(x,y)=P(X\le x,Y\le y)$ is the probability that the pair $(X,Y)$ will lie inside the infinite rectangular region that has its top-right corner at $(x,y)$ and whose sides are parallel to the coordinate axes.

Let's sketch the region corresponding to the probability we wish to find.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14211556/assets/0378964a9f167554e4faeba228ebae485de94dda83fbd6704a864a06b8abe77a.png)

Geometrically, this region can be obtained by taking the infinite rectangle that has its top-right corner at $(1,5)$ (the blue region below) and *subtracting* the infinite rectangle that has its top-right corner at $(-2,5)$ (the red region below).

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14211556/assets/9079baa6464df773cacb820a6bb4a8e2b8f4ecc19755619a9b5c191a0c48507f.png)

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-2\le X\le 1,Y\le 5) & =\overset{\text{top-right corner at }(1,5)}{\overset{⏞}{P(X\le 1,Y\le 5)}}-\overset{\text{top-right corner at }(-2,5)}{\overset{⏞}{P(X\le -2,Y\le 5)}} \\  & =F(1,5)-F(-2,5) \\  & =0.63-0.27 \\  & =0.36.\end{aligned}
$$
